verdict.rationale: Codex ships its own plugin browser (`/plugins` in the CLI, a Plugins tab in the app) for browsing and installing from configured marketplaces, backed by one universal plugin directory. A runtime probe confirmed a public, keylessly fetchable curated marketplace manifest ('Codex official') that lists plugins with categories, source paths and install policies, and curated skills can be installed by name. missing for 10: explicit documentation of in-catalog search or filtering (browsing is documented, search is not).

support.subject: As a developer, I can browse or search a catalog of available skills — a registry, leaderboard, or marketplace listing — before installing anything

citations.quote: In Codex CLI, enter `/plugins` to open the plugin browser. Install a plugin from a configured marketplace, then start a new session before using its bundled skills or tools.
Open the Plugins tab to browse and install plugins.
Both products use one universal plugin directory, so the same public plugins are discoverable from their supported surfaces.
a public JSON catalog ('openai-curated', display name 'Codex official') listing plugins with source paths and installation/authentication policies.
Curated skills can be installed by name (defaults to `skills/.curated`)
